podcast: Diamond Hands Podcast with Leslie Tracey

233fb2ea5f.q: What is Sighten's one core policy that guides all employee decisions?
233fb2ea5f.a: Sighten has one policy: do the right thing. Aaron Burton explains that if you hire people to do the right thing and they make mistakes, that is not bad—repeating mistakes is bad. The company avoids creating additional bureaucratic rules and instead trusts employees to act with integrity based on this single principle.

baf42e0dec.q: What are the top three credos in Sighten's leadership framework?
baf42e0dec.a: The top three credos are: trust and value people, have a heart and be kind and lead with love, and be grateful and show gratitude. Burton explains these came from a culture task force about 10 years ago and are printed on a credo card that all Sighten leaders carry and wear, symbolized by a blue heart at company events.

7f31043d83.q: How did Sighten handle workforce layoffs during the COVID-19 pandemic?
7f31043d83.a: During COVID, Sighten did not lay off a single person. Burton states this was one of their biggest advantages coming out of COVID because they operated like a family in practice, not just in theory. The decision reflected their philosophy that you don't fire people just because business conditions worsen.

fb83332095.q: What practical method does Sighten's leadership teach for building gratitude daily?
fb83332095.a: Burton recommends starting each day by saying 'I'm grateful to be alive' and feeding your mind something positive in the first five minutes after waking. Similarly, the last five minutes before bed should also be positive. He also references a Northwestern study showing that sitting in cubicles next to successful people makes you more likely to be successful.

407307a142.q: Why does Sighten promote internal candidates to senior leadership rather than hiring external leaders?
407307a142.a: Sighten is very protective about who becomes a leader because internal promotion ensures people have time to learn the company's culture and values. Burton states that almost every senior leader came up from a lower rank, which gives them a competitive advantage and prevents the company from mixing in external leaders who haven't been taught how Sighten operates.
